title: Stay on the Path: A Week in the Swiss National Park

bestPeriod.note: Chamanna Cluozza opens roughly mid-June to mid-October only; the Val Trupchun red deer rut in September draws the heaviest foot traffic of the year.

summary: A week inside the strictest nature reserve in the Alps: marked paths only, nothing picked, no camping and no dogs, from Zernez to a hut with no road and Val Trupchun's ibex and red deer.
hook: Founded in 1914, the Swiss National Park is the oldest in the Alps and by far the strictest: leaving the marked path is forbidden everywhere, picking anything — a flower, a mushroom, a pinecone — is forbidden everywhere, and dogs, camping, cycling off the pass road and fires are all simply not allowed. What that discipline buys you is an ecosystem left almost entirely alone for over a century: bearded vultures reintroduced from nothing, ibex on the scree in plain sight, and Val Trupchun's red deer herds that draw wildlife watchers from across Switzerland every September.

snapshot.Base(s): Zernez (5 nights), Chamanna Cluozza (1 night), Zernez again (1 night)
snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: approx. 60–70 km walking, 3,000–3,400 m cumulative ascent; marked mountain path throughout, no off-path travel permitted anywhere
snapshot.Getting There: Zurich (ZRH) → Rhaetian Railway via Chur and the Vereina line to Zernez (approx. 3h30)
snapshot.Who It Suits: Disciplined, patient walkers who want serious wildlife and can accept strict rules without exception

itinerary.title: Zurich to Zernez
itinerary.morning: Train from Zurich via Chur, through the Vereina tunnel, to Zernez — no car is needed anywhere on this trip, and the park itself has no internal road network beyond the Ofenpass (Pass dal Fuorn) that skirts its southern edge.
itinerary.afternoon: Visit the Nationalparkzentrum in Zernez, the park's excellent visitor centre, before entering — it explains the rule set clearly and is worth the hour, since rangers assume you have read it.
itinerary.evening: Settle into Zernez; the village is small but has several restaurants and a supermarket, the last full resupply point before several days of hut and trail food.
itinerary.dayStats: 4 km, negligible vert. Village paths. Water: Zernez shops. Bail-out: village is the base itself.

itinerary.title: Val Trupchun: ibex, deer and the park's best wildlife valley
itinerary.morning: Bus to S-chanf and the Val Trupchun trailhead, then walk in along the marked valley path — no vehicle goes further than the car park.
itinerary.afternoon: Val Trupchun is the park's best wildlife valley: ibex work the scree above the path in full view, red deer graze the floor, and in September the rut is loud and constant. Stay strictly on the marked path — rangers patrol here specifically because of the crowds it draws.
itinerary.dayStats: 18 km, 550 m vert. Marked valley path, well-graded, no exposure. Water: none inside the park — carry 2 L, since no picking, foraging or off-trail refill is permitted and streams are not treated water sources. Bail-out: the valley path is a straightforward there-and-back to the trailhead at any point.

itinerary.title: Il Fuorn and the Ofenpass forests
itinerary.morning: Bus along the Ofenpass road to Il Fuorn, where the Parc Naziunal's own historic hotel sits directly inside the park boundary — one of the very few permitted buildings within it.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk one of the marked loop trails from Il Fuorn through old-growth stone-pine and larch forest, some of the least disturbed subalpine forest in the Alps, precisely because a century of strict protection has kept it that way.
itinerary.evening: Bus back to Zernez, or dine at Il Fuorn's hotel restaurant before returning.
itinerary.dayStats: 14 km, 400 m vert. Marked forest path. Water: Il Fuorn hotel. Bail-out: the Ofenpass road bus runs regularly in both directions.

itinerary.title: Walk in to Chamanna Cluozza
itinerary.morning: Full pack on. Walk from Zernez (or a short bus hop to Punt la Drossa) along the marked path into the Cluozza valley, climbing steadily through forest and open slope.
itinerary.afternoon: Arrive at Chamanna Cluozza (1,882 m), the only overnight accommodation inside the park and reachable solely on foot — no road comes near it. It runs off-grid: solar power for lighting, water piped from a mountain source, a dry or low-flush toilet system, and a strict carry-out policy for anything you bring in that isn't food waste handled by the hut itself.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at the hut (advance booking essential; the hut sells out on clear-forecast weekends in its short season). No fires, no dogs, and quiet hours are taken seriously here.
itinerary.dayStats: 12 km, 750 m ascent from Zernez. Marked mountain path, some steeper switchbacks, no technical exposure. Water: none en route, arrive with a full bottle — refill at the hut. Bail-out: the path back down to Zernez is the same trail, roughly 2.5–3 hours.

itinerary.title: A quiet day around Cluozza, then back to Zernez
itinerary.morning: A short marked loop above the hut for views over the Cluozza gorge and, with luck, bearded vultures riding the thermals — the species was reintroduced to the Alps starting in 1991, with the Engadin among the first release sites, and sightings here are genuinely common, not a rarity to hope for.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend the marked path back to Zernez, retracing the previous day's route.
itinerary.evening: A full dinner and a proper bed in Zernez after the hut's simpler facilities.
itinerary.dayStats: 12 km, 750 m descent. Marked mountain path. Water: hut supply at the start, Zernez at the end. Bail-out: the descent path has no alternative exits — commit to the full return once started.

itinerary.title: S-charl valley and Zernez museum
itinerary.morning: Bus to S-charl, a quiet side valley with a small hamlet and a history of silver mining, sitting just outside the park's strictest core zone with a gentler network of marked paths.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk one of the S-charl loops, then return to Zernez for a lighter final full day before departure.
itinerary.evening: Return to the Nationalparkzentrum's exhibition for anything missed on arrival, or a last dinner in Zernez.
itinerary.dayStats: 14 km, 400 m vert. Marked path, gentle grades. Water: S-charl hamlet. Bail-out: the S-charl postbus runs on a fixed schedule back to Scuol or Zernez.

itinerary.title: Zernez to Zurich
itinerary.morning: A short valley walk near Zernez if time allows, otherwise pack and confirm the return train.
itinerary.afternoon: Rhaetian Railway back to Zurich via Chur.
itinerary.dayStats: Transfer day, short optional walk only.

accommodationStrategy.name: Guesthouse in Zernez
accommodationStrategy.description: The obvious base: on the railway line, at the Nationalparkzentrum's doorstep, and the last point with a full supermarket and pharmacy before the park's interior. Book ahead for September, when rut-season wildlife watchers fill the village.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 6–8 weeks ahead for September; 3–4 weeks otherwise.

accommodationStrategy.name: Chamanna Cluozza
accommodationStrategy.description: The only overnight accommodation permitted inside the park, reached on foot only, with a short season (roughly mid-June to mid-October) dictated by snow and staffing. Off-grid facilities: solar lighting, piped mountain-source water, and a low-impact toilet system; bring a sleeping-bag liner, since bedding at Swiss huts is typically a shared dormitory mattress and blanket only.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 8–10 weeks ahead — this is the single hardest reservation of the trip and the hut fills months out for peak-season weekends.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Il Fuorn
accommodationStrategy.description: One of the only buildings permitted inside the park boundary, useful as an alternative or additional night if Chamanna Cluozza is unavailable, with easier road access via the Ofenpass bus and a proper restaurant.

logistics.emergency: 112 pan-European, or Switzerland's Rega mountain rescue on 1414. Note the signal gaps in the Cluozza valley to hut staff on arrival — they have radio contact.
logistics.money: Swiss franc (CHF); cards work widely, including at Cluozza and Il Fuorn, but carry cash as backup where connectivity is unreliable.

other.label: Access
other.text: Zernez is reached entirely by rail, no 4x4 needed; within the park, movement is on foot only, since private vehicles are restricted to the Ofenpass through-road and its trailhead car parks. Chamanna Cluozza has no vehicle access in any season.

other.label: Isolation level
other.text: The nearest full shop, pharmacy and doctor are in Zernez; once inside the park, there is no resupply beyond the Il Fuorn hotel and the Cluozza hut kitchen. Signal is reliable in Zernez and along the Ofenpass but patchy to absent in Val Trupchun and around Cluozza — treat the park interior as out of contact.

other.label: Resupply
other.text: Zernez has a Coop or Volg-style general store; buy everything needed for hut days there.

other.label: Foraging and fire law — the strictest in this itinerary
other.text: Nothing may be picked anywhere: no flowers, berries, mushrooms, wood or rocks. Marked paths only, enforced by wardens with real fines. Dogs are not permitted anywhere, including on a lead. Camping, bivouacking, off-road cycling, drones and open fires are all prohibited, as is swimming in the park's streams and lakes.

other.label: Wildlife
other.text: Ibex and bearded vulture are the signature sightings, best looked for on the open scree and thermals above Val Trupchun and the Cluozza gorge; the red deer rut runs through September and draws the year's biggest crowds to Val Trupchun. Marmots are common at lower elevations.

other.label: Ticks
other.text: Graubünden carries TBE risk at lower elevations; vaccination or careful checks are sensible for S-charl and the lower Cluozza valley.

proTips: Book Chamanna Cluozza first — its short season and single-hut status inside the whole park make it the binding constraint on the week.
Walk Val Trupchun on a weekday if possible; September weekends draw dedicated wildlife-watching groups and the trailhead car park fills early.
Bring your own binoculars rather than relying on shared hut equipment — sightings reward patience, not proximity, which the rules prohibit anyway.
Read the park's rule leaflet, free at the Nationalparkzentrum and every trailhead board, before Day 2 — rangers do check.
S-charl on Day 6 sits just outside the strictest core and feels noticeably gentler — a good rest day after the core-zone discipline.
Ask the Nationalparkzentrum for that week's ranger-guided walk schedule — the only way to get expert spotting without leaving the marked path.
Aim for a weekday arrival at Cluozza; the small dining room gets genuinely crowded on a clear Friday or Saturday in high season.

packingNotes: A sleeping-bag liner for Chamanna Cluozza's dormitory bedding.
2 L water carrying capacity for Val Trupchun and the Cluozza approach, since no reliable refill exists on either trail.
A proper rain shell — Engadin afternoon storms build quickly even on a clear-forecast morning.
Binoculars, non-negotiable for this trip given the no-approach wildlife rules.
Sturdy walking boots with good grip for the steeper Cluozza switchbacks.
A headtorch for the hut, where lighting is solar and minimal after dark.
Swiss francs in cash as backup for the hut and Il Fuorn.
A printed copy of your Cluozza hut booking confirmation, since signal there is unreliable.
Warm layers even in July — Cluozza sits near 1,900 m and nights are cold regardless of valley-floor weather.
whatCouldGoWrong: **Chamanna Cluozza is fully booked.** Fallback: day-hike into the Cluozza valley from Zernez and back without the overnight, basing at Il Fuorn or Zernez instead.

**A storm breaks over the Cluozza approach.** Fallback: the marked path has no shelter for long stretches; turn back to Zernez rather than push on, since off-path shortcuts to escape weather are also against the rules.
**Val Trupchun is restricted on a peak rut-season weekend.** Fallback: check the Nationalparkzentrum's notice board and shift the visit to a weekday, or substitute S-charl.
**A ranger cites you for leaving the path or bringing a dog.** These rules are absolute and fined — the only real fallback is not testing them.
**Signal loss at Cluozza delays confirming a return connection.** Fallback: confirm the Zernez–Zurich train before walking in.
